newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 27.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company.

- 39 DEAD IN MASS SUICIDE Sheriff's deputies in California have discovered the bodies of 39 young men in a San Diego mansion. It is thought the 39 bodies represent a mass suicide by members of a cult knwn as WW Higher Source.

- DFS CHIEF SEEKS TO REVIVE SALE TO LVMH Robert Miller, the billionaire founder of duty free shops group DFS, is seeking an independent arbitrator after LVMH withdrew from the purchase of his stake in DFS. Miller wants to restart talks with LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault, who pulled out of the deal to buy Miller's holding for around 980m stg last week.

- US WARNING SHOT HITS THE GREENBACK The dollar fell during the overnight Asian trading session, following a warning from the US Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers that the dollar's strength could help Japan's trade surplus "expand substantially".

- CLUBS BID DATE RETHINK Financiers are advising London Clubs International to shorten the offer period, which ends on May 2, in its 196m stg hostile bid for Capital Corporation. There is concern that the clash with the General Election date would cause administrative problems.

- MURDOCH EARMARKS 600M STG FOR TV DEAL Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation is having talks in the US, which could pave the way to spending up to 1bn dollars (600m stg) on expanding its sports broadcast holdings. In a move designed to restore good relations with erstwhile American partner TeleCommunications Inc (TCI), News Corp is considering buying its stakes in a dozen regional and cable television networks around the US.
